thread:
jordan_cs: FYI escalating: BlueFish Health is seeing a clear quality regression after yesterday's quant profile rollout to their Dedicated pool. Customer says outputs are missing steps and hallucinating in clinical note summarization. Putting the excerpts and repro below. Marking as P1 for now.

jordan_cs: Example (customer-provided):
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "rw/fastgen-13b-v1",
  "quant_profile": "int8-medical-v2",
  "input": "Summarize this patient visit: Patient presented with chest pain, ECG showed no ischemia, discharged with follow-up..."
}
```

jordan_cs: Customer output (new):
"Patient had significant cardiac event and was admitted for observation."

jordan_cs: Expected (pre-rollout baseline fp16):
"Patient presented with chest pain; ECG did not indicate ischemia. Discharged with outpatient follow-up; advised to return if symptoms worsen."

jordan_cs: They attached a longer prompt set and claim >30% drop in factual precision on our internal metric. They can reproduce against their Dedicated pool id d-03a7 and mention it started ~2026-03-03 02:10 UTC.

priya_eng: Thanks, noted. Quick q: did they pin a specific model version? Jordan, can you confirm config exactly — model + quant_profile + any runtime overrides?

jordan_cs: They provided a screenshot of the call: model=rw/fastgen-13b-v1, quant_profile=int8-medical-v2, runtime_flags: {"kv_cache_policy":"dynamic","token_batching":"auto"}. No manual overrides beyond that.

eli_sre: I see a spike in error/sec and a small uptick in latency for d-03a7 around that time but nothing huge. However, a canary update to quant profiles rolled through Dedicated yesterday at 02:00 UTC — @kai_infra can you confirm rollout scope?

kai_infra: deploy-bot reported the rollout. Canary target was Dedicated pools with tag "medical"; 5% -> 25% -> 100% over ~2h. I still have the deploy logs:
```
deploy-bot: canary quant profile rollout started: profile=int8-medical-v2, targets=[tag:medical], phases=[5,25,100], start=2026-03-03T01:15:00Z
```

matt_research: Larger context: int8-medical-v2 is a more aggressive quantization profile we CTA'd for lower-latency on common seq lengths. It uses asymmetric quant scales on select weight groups and an fp32 residual path for attention. We did validation on our eval sets but may have gaps in clinical paraphrase coverage.

priya_eng: Can we reproduce locally with a snapshot of the same profile? If so we should A/B compare outputs: fp16 baseline vs int8 profile. Matt, can your bench run the customer's prompt set at scale?

matt_research: Yes, I can run that. Jordan: please upload the customer's prompt set to the shared S3 (or paste a small sample here). Also need the exact seed/temperature used.

jordan_cs: Uploaded to s3://redwood-escalations/bluefish/2026-03-03/prompts.jsonl. Temp=0.0, top_p=0.85. They used a short context window (~512 tokens).

eli_sre: While matt runs the eval, can we temporarily mitigate for the customer? Options: 1) Force the pool to fall back to fp16 model variant, 2) Pin quant_profile back to int8-medical-v1 for their Dedicated pool, or 3) Route their traffic to Hosted until we triage. Thoughts? @kai_infra

kai_infra: Quickest for mitigation is to pin their Dedicated pool to a safe profile. I can apply a pool override that forces quant_profile=fp16-baseline for d-03a7. That will take ~3 min and cause a brief capacity rebalance. Need cs approval.

jordan_cs: Customer wants minimal disruption but will accept a short swap. Please proceed with pin if you think it's safe.

kai_infra: Proceeding now. I’ll annotate rollback window and notify.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued: pool=d-03a7, set quant_profile=fp16-baseline, initiated_by=kai_infra, job_id=rb-7291

eli_sre: Noted. Matt: any preliminary results from the eval run?

matt_research: Quick A/B (50 prompts) — preliminary numbers: factual precision drop from 0.88 -> 0.61 on int8-medical-v2 for this set. Confidence intervals still wide but direction is consistent. Example failures are mainly facts being "compressed" into more generic or hallucinated claims when numbers/dates are present. I’ll push full 1k prompt run; ETA ~45m.

priya_eng: This suggests quantization-induced numerical drift in certain weight groups affecting the decoder logits. Can you capture logits and softmax temperature differences for failed examples? Also include KV-cache traces if possible.

matt_research: Will capture. Also noticed one interesting pattern: when input contains short lists (medications, vitals), int8 outputs tend to merge items or invent additional meds.

eli_sre: Rollback to fp16 completed. Monitoring customer pool now.

deploy-bot: rollback job complete: rb-7291, status=success, completed_at=2026-03-03T02:22:14Z

jordan_cs: Customer confirmed immediate improvement on a quick test — they said summaries look closer to baseline. Marking mitigation = successful. They've asked for root cause and ETA to re-introduce a safe profile.

priya_eng: Next steps: (1) Matt to produce detailed A/B artifacts (logits, token-level diffs), (2) Eng to add targeted quantization tests for clinical paraphrase categories, (3) Infra to hold profile rollout for "medical" tag until signoff. Assigning owners: matt_research (A/B artifacts), priya_eng (test coverage + patch), kai_infra (hold rollout + rollback plan).

matt_research: Will have artifacts + initial hypothesis (asymmetric scale overflow in group G12) in ~6 hours. I also want to run the same prompts on fp8_experimental to see if fp8 reduces the drift.

kai_infra: I created a temporary hold: rollout_hold[tag=medical]=true. Will not reapply int8-medical-v2 until engineering says otherwise.

priya_eng: Also flagging on the release notes that this profile is experimental for clinical workloads. We need a more robust QA gate.

jordan_cs: Customer asked for a postmortem and a timeline. I'll tell them we'll send a detailed RCA within 48 hours and provide a temporary pin until that time.

eli_sre: Logging action items in incidents channel and creating an incident ticket now.

deploy-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1103, severity=P1, owner=priya_eng, summary=quant-profile regression affecting Dedicated medical pools

matt_research: Uploading A/B artifacts to s3://redwood-escalations/bluefish/2026-03-03/ab_artifacts.tar.gz when done. Preliminary note: fp8_experimental reduces factual drop to 0.80 on the 50-sample run — promising but we need full pass.

priya_eng: If fp8 looks better, we can iterate a new profile int8-medical-v2a or introduce fp8-medical-stable. But first: reproduce, instrument, and a small targeted canary with customer opt-in.

jordan_cs: I'll coordinate customer opt-in for canary. They prefer a narrow test & rollback window.

eli_sre: Closing loop until artifacts arrive. Current state: mitigation applied, incident created, owners assigned.

priya_eng: Thanks everyone. Please paste any raw failed samples in-channel (sanitize PHI) or point to S3. I'll take lead on test additions and a recommended change to quantization group scaling.

matt_research: Uploaded artifacts + raw diffs (PHI redacted). Link: s3://redwood-escalations/bluefish/2026-03-03/ab_artifacts.tar.gz

jordan_cs: Customer replied: "Thanks, we saw immediate improvement after rollback; we'll wait for your test results before we do any further testing." :thumbsup:

eli_sre: Will keep monitoring and will ping if any regression reappears.

priya_eng: I’ll draft the RCA and propose a gated rollout plan: (a) larger eval suite including clinical paraphrase and list handling, (b) small customer canary opt-in, (c) automatic rollback if token-level precision delta > 0.1.

jordan_cs: Great. I’ll update the customer and mark this thread as P1 Escalation active -> mitigated (rolled back). Will reopen if new data appears.

kai_infra: Note: we should add a runtime metric for token-precision-delta so infra can auto-detect these regressions next time.

priya_eng: Agreed. Starting a ticket for that metric integration.

jordan_cs: Thanks all. Close for now until RCA done.
